# Shared definitions

Building blocks shared by the overlay, module overlay, pluggable, rack and pack schemas.

Schema: [`danbyte/schema/common.schema.json`](../../schema/common.schema.json) (danbyte-library/v1).


## Definitions

### format

The library format this file is written for. Optional; the tools write it, and a later format will change the value.

Type: `"danbyte-library/v1"`

### why

Why Danbyte adds or changes this: required on every addition and removal, so a reviewer sees it was deliberate and can offer it upstream to NetBox. Name the source (install guide, data sheet, the hardware itself).

Type: string

Example:

```yaml
StackPower receptacle on the rear panel (Cisco C9300 HIG); upstream has no StackPower ports
...
```

### name

A component name, exactly as in the NetBox YAML (`{module}` placeholders included).

Type: string

### partNumber

A vendor part number, exactly as the vendor prints it.

Type: string

### assetPath

A file under `danbyte/`, relative to it (normally `assets/<Vendor>/<file>`). No `..`, no absolute paths.

Type: string (pattern)

### glbPath

A binary glTF 2.0 file (`.glb`) under `danbyte/`, normally `assets/<Vendor>/<PART>.glb`. Stored with Git LFS.

Type: [assetPath](#assetpath)

### imagePath

A WebP or PNG image under `danbyte/`, normally `assets/<Vendor>/<PART>.<face>.webp`. Stored with Git LFS.

Type: [assetPath](#assetpath)

### ledBinding

What lights one LED. `source` is where its state comes from; `modules.status` takes the worst status of the modules in matching bays (`bays:`, or inline as `"modules.status: PS-*"`); `only` lights it only in those colours (a failure LED: `[red]`).

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | one of `device.status`, `device.locate`, `module.status`, `modules.status`, `interface.oper_status`, `none` or string (pattern) | yes | device.status, device.locate, module.status, modules.status, interface.oper_status, or none (a decorative LED that stays off). |
| `bays` | list of string |  | modules.status only: the bay names or globs it reads. |
| `only` | list of one of `green`, `amber`, `red`, `blue` |  | Light the LED only in these colours. |

### model3d

The 3D model of a device or module type (export spec §1-§8). Danbyte assembles a device from its chassis file plus one file per installed module, placed at the chassis' `bay:` empties, and lights `led:` meshes from live status.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | [glbPath](#glbpath) | yes | The full-detail model. Budgets: chassis ≤ 150,000 triangles, module ≤ 30,000; ≤ 8 MB. |
| `far` | [glbPath](#glbpath) |  | The far-distance copy: same origin, outer size and `bay:` / `empty:` / `led:` names. Budgets: chassis ≤ 15,000 triangles, module ≤ 3,000; ≤ 1 MB. |
| `empty` | one of `filler`, `hole`, `nothing` |  | What an empty bay shows: the model's `empty:` filler plate, a dark hole, or nothing. |
| `fit` | one of `auto`, `native` |  | `auto` fits the model to the type's size; `native` keeps the model's own size. |
| `up` | one of `y`, `z` |  | The model's up axis, when not glTF's Y. |
| `front` | one of `+z`, `-z`, `+x`, `-x` |  | The axis the model's front faces, when not +Z. |
| `leds` | map of name → [ledBinding](#ledbinding) |  | LED id → binding. Keys are the `led:` mesh names without `led:`; `port:*` covers every `led:port:` LED. An LED without an entry stays off. |
| `renders` | [renders](#renders) |  | Device types: face photos rendered in Blender from the model (export spec §12). Danbyte stores them as the type's photos and places its ports on them. |

Example:

```yaml
file: assets/Cisco/C9300-24P.glb
far: assets/Cisco/C9300-24P.far.glb
empty: filler
leds:
  SYS: {source: device.status}
  port:*: {source: interface.oper_status}
```

### renders

Device types: face photos rendered in Blender from the model (export spec §12). Danbyte stores them as the type's photos and places its ports on them.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `front` | [imagePath](#imagepath) |  | A WebP or PNG image under `danbyte/`, normally `assets/<Vendor>/<PART>.<face>.webp`. Stored with Git LFS. |
| `rear` | [imagePath](#imagepath) |  | A WebP or PNG image under `danbyte/`, normally `assets/<Vendor>/<PART>.<face>.webp`. Stored with Git LFS. |
| `iso` | [imagePath](#imagepath) |  | Three-quarter view; the catalog's thumbnail. |
| `model_sha256` | string (pattern) |  | SHA-256 of the `file` glb the photos were rendered from; `validate` checks it matches. |
| `modules` | map of name → [partNumber](#partnumber) |  | Bay name → module part number installed in the render. |

### rackMount

How the device sits on a rack's rails (export spec §3, §8 "Rack mounting"). Danbyte puts the ear plane on the rack's front rail and the faceplate at the chosen position's offset.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ears` | boolean |  | false: no rack ears (shelf, sliding rails, free-standing). Default true. |
| `positions` | mapping |  | Ear positions the install guide offers: faceplate in front of the ear plane, in mm (+ toward the rack front; a recessed front fitting is negative). |
| `default` | one of `front`, `mid`, `rear` |  | The fitting the box ships with. |
| `rails` | one of `none`, `fixed`, `sliding` |  | The rail kit it is meant for. |

#### rackMount.positions

Ear positions the install guide offers: faceplate in front of the ear plane, in mm (+ toward the rack front; a recessed front fitting is negative).

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `front` | integer (-2000–2000) |  |  |
| `mid` | integer (-2000–2000) |  |  |
| `rear` | integer (-2000–2000) |  |  |

Example:

```yaml
ears: true
positions: {front: 0, rear: 430}
default: front
rails: none
```

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after` | [name](#name) |  | Insert right after this existing component (default: at the end of the list). |
| `before` | [name](#name) |  | Insert right before this existing component. |

Type: list of mapping

### interfacePatch

Fields to change on an interface that upstream already has, found by its name. Only the fields given change; `why` is optional on a change.

Also takes the keys of [interfaceFields](#interfacefields).

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `why` | [why](#why) |  | Why Danbyte adds or changes this: required on every addition and removal, so a reviewer sees it was deliberate and can offer it upstream to NetBox. Name the source (install guide, data sheet, the hardware itself). |

### interfaceAdd

An interface upstream lacks, in NetBox's own fields plus `why`. Added at the end of the list unless `after` / `before` say where.

Also takes the keys of [interfaceFields](#interfacefields), [placement](#placement).

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | [name](#name) | yes | A component name, exactly as in the NetBox YAML (`{module}` placeholders included). |
| `why` | [why](#why) | yes | Why Danbyte adds or changes this: required on every addition and removal, so a reviewer sees it was deliberate and can offer it upstream to NetBox. Name the source (install guide, data sheet, the hardware itself). |

| *other keys* | [inventoryItemPatch](#inventoryitempatch) | | Fields to change on an inventory item that upstream already has, found by its name. Only the fields given change; `why` is optional on a change. |

### extensionTypes

Port types Danbyte reads that NetBox doesn't list yet, by component class. A merged record may use them although NetBox's own schema would refuse them; `validate` accepts exactly these. Offer them upstream when NetBox would take them.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `power-port` | one of `cisco-stackpower` |  | `cisco-stackpower`: a Cisco StackPower receptacle (Catalyst 9300 / 9300X). It carries power between stack members, so it is a power port, not an interface. |
